components.cost_effect: One block-gradient query and update, plus separately charged sampling and arithmetic.
components.goal: Obtain expected descent using one selected block gradient per iteration.
components.name: Fixed weighted sampling and quadratic-model block step
components.operation: Draw i with p_i=L_i^alpha/S_alpha, then apply -g_i/L_i in that block.
components.requires: Known positive coordinate constants, Euclidean block geometry and exact gradients.

variants.cost: K exact selected block-gradient queries, K random block draws and K block updates. Weight normalization and sampling data structures are separate preprocessing. Sampling, arithmetic, memory traffic and any residual maintenance are separately charged. An update in block i touches n_i scalar entries. Optional function values are separately charged. No universal arithmetic cost for a block-gradient query, free full gradient or runtime speedup factor is asserted.

variants.name: Euclidean RCDM(alpha,x0)
variants.output: Last iterate x_K. The source also discusses (x_K,f(x_K)); obtaining the value requires a separately charged function-value evaluation when unavailable.
public_inputs: n>=1 coordinate blocks, positive integer dimensions n_i, N=sum_i n_i and embeddings U_i.
Deterministic x0 in R^N, known finite L_i>0, fixed alpha in R and integer horizon K>=0.
variants.query_and_update: For t=0,...,K-1, draw i_t using fresh randomness with conditional probability P(i_t=i | past)=p_i. Query g=U_i_t^T grad f(x_t). Set x_{t+1}^(i_t)=x_t^(i_t)-g/L_i_t and leave all other blocks unchanged. Equivalently x_{t+1}=x_t-U_i_t g/L_i_t. This is the source quadratic-model step specialized to Euclidean norms, not exact block minimization.
variants.requirements: Convex differentiable f:R^N->R; exact g_i(x)=U_i^T grad f(x); Euclidean coordinate smoothness ||g_i(x+U_i h)-g_i(x)||_2<=L_i||h||_2 for every i,x,h. The linked finite performance bound additionally retains nonempty bounded X* and finite R_{1-alpha}(x0).
variants.state_and_initialization: Store x=x0 and the block partition. Compute w_i=L_i^alpha, S_alpha=sum_i w_i and p_i=w_i/S_alpha. No optimizer, f* or radius is needed for a fixed-horizon run.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Use fixed steps 1/L_i and fixed alpha; stop after K updates. No line search, restart or objective-based stopping is required. Selecting a target-accuracy horizon requires a valid public radius bound; that information is not supplied by the selected block-gradient oracle.
